title: A coroutine scheduler
description:
Game engines run many small scripts at once: a guard patrols, a door opens after three seconds, a bird sings now and then. Each script is written as a simple sequence, and a scheduler gives every script a turn on every tick. Build that scheduler as a module that returns a `Scheduler` class.

```lua-norun
local s = Scheduler.new()
s:spawn("door", function(sched)
    sched:log("closing")
    coroutine.yield(3)          -- sleep for 3 ticks
    sched:log("open")
end)
s:run()
```

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `Scheduler.new()` | a scheduler at tick 0 with no tasks |
| `s:spawn(name, fn)` | adds a task; it first runs on the next tick that runs. `fn` receives the scheduler |
| `s:now()` | the current tick |
| `s:log(text)` | records `"<tick> <task name>: <text>"`; called from inside a task |
| `s:run(max_ticks)` | runs ticks 1, 2, 3, ... until no task is left, or until `max_ticks` ticks have run (if given). Returns the number of the last tick that ran |
| `s:entries()` | the log, a list of strings, in order |
| `s:finished()` | names of the tasks that ended, in the order they ended |
| `s:errors()` | `"<task name>: <message>"` for each task that raised an error, in order |

Rules for each tick:
1. The tick number goes up by one.
2. Every task that is awake runs, in the order the tasks were spawned, until it yields or ends.
3. A task that yields `n` sleeps for `n` ticks: yielding 1 (or yielding with no value) means it runs again on the next tick, yielding 3 means it next runs 3 ticks later.
4. A task that ends is removed and added to `finished`. A task that raises an error is removed and its error added to `errors`; the other tasks carry on.
5. A task spawned while a tick is running first runs on the next tick.

solution.solution.lua:
local Scheduler = {}
Scheduler.__index = Scheduler

function Scheduler.new()
    return setmetatable({ tick = 0, tasks = {}, log_lines = {}, done = {}, failed = {}, current = nil }, Scheduler)
end

function Scheduler:spawn(name, fn)
    self.tasks[#self.tasks + 1] = { name = name, co = coroutine.create(fn), wake = self.tick + 1, started = false }
end

function Scheduler:now()
    return self.tick
end

function Scheduler:log(text)
    local who = self.current and self.current.name or "?"
    self.log_lines[#self.log_lines + 1] = self.tick .. " " .. who .. ": " .. text
end

function Scheduler:run(max_ticks)
    local ran = 0
    while #self.tasks > 0 and (not max_ticks or ran < max_ticks) do
        self.tick = self.tick + 1
        ran = ran + 1
        local running = {}
        for i, task in ipairs(self.tasks) do running[i] = task end
        for _, task in ipairs(running) do
            if task.wake <= self.tick then
                self.current = task
                local ok, result
                if task.started then
                    ok, result = coroutine.resume(task.co)
                else
                    task.started = true
                    ok, result = coroutine.resume(task.co, self)
                end
                self.current = nil
                if not ok then
                    task.gone = true
                    self.failed[#self.failed + 1] = task.name .. ": " .. tostring(result)
                elseif coroutine.status(task.co) == "dead" then
                    task.gone = true
                    self.done[#self.done + 1] = task.name
                else
                    task.wake = self.tick + (tonumber(result) or 1)
                end
            end
        end
        local keep = {}
        for _, task in ipairs(self.tasks) do
            if not task.gone then keep[#keep + 1] = task end
        end
        self.tasks = keep
    end
    return self.tick
end

function Scheduler:entries()
    return self.log_lines
end

function Scheduler:finished()
    return self.done
end

function Scheduler:errors()
    return self.failed
end

return Scheduler

hints: Keep one record per task: `{ name, co = coroutine.create(fn), wake = <tick to run next> }`. The first `resume` passes the scheduler as the function's argument; later ones pass nothing.
What `coroutine.yield(n)` yields comes back as the second result of `coroutine.resume`. A task that yielded nothing gives `nil`: treat it as 1.
Loop over a copy of the task list during a tick, so tasks spawned meanwhile wait for the next one, and remove finished tasks after the tick.
requirements: Tasks take turns in spawn order and sleep for the ticks they yield.
The log, finished and errors lists match the rules.
run stops when no tasks are left, or at max_ticks.
stretch:
- Add `sched:wait_until(condition)`: a task sleeps until a function returns true.
- Add `s:cancel(name)`.
unitTests:
local Scheduler = require("solution")

test("one task that sleeps", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    s:spawn("door", function(sched)
        sched:log("closing")
        coroutine.yield(3)
        sched:log("open")
    end)
    check_eq(s:run(), 4)
    check_eq(s:entries(), { "1 door: closing", "4 door: open" })
    check_eq(s:finished(), { "door" })
end)

test("tasks take turns in spawn order", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    s:spawn("guard", function(sched)
        sched:log("left"); coroutine.yield(2)
        sched:log("right"); coroutine.yield(2)
        sched:log("done")
    end)
    s:spawn("bird", function(sched)
        for i = 1, 3 do sched:log("tweet " .. i); coroutine.yield() end
    end)
    check_eq(s:run(), 5)
    check_eq(s:entries(), { "1 guard: left", "1 bird: tweet 1", "2 bird: tweet 2", "3 guard: right", "3 bird: tweet 3", "5 guard: done" })
    check_eq(s:finished(), { "bird", "guard" })
end)

test("now and the task argument", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    local seen = {}
    s:spawn("clock", function(sched)
        check(sched == s, "the task receives the scheduler")
        for _ = 1, 3 do seen[#seen + 1] = sched:now(); coroutine.yield(2) end
    end)
    s:run()
    check_eq(seen, { 1, 3, 5 })
end)

test("a failing task does not stop the others", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    s:spawn("bad", function(sched) coroutine.yield(); error("broken", 0) end)
    s:spawn("good", function(sched) coroutine.yield(); coroutine.yield(); sched:log("still here") end)
    s:run()
    check_eq(s:errors(), { "bad: broken" })
    check_eq(s:finished(), { "good" })
    check_eq(s:entries(), { "3 good: still here" })
end)

test("tasks spawned during a tick start on the next one", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    s:spawn("parent", function(sched)
        sched:log("spawning")
        sched:spawn("child", function(c) c:log("hello") end)
        sched:log("spawned")
    end)
    check_eq(s:run(), 2)
    check_eq(s:entries(), { "1 parent: spawning", "1 parent: spawned", "2 child: hello" })
    check_eq(s:finished(), { "parent", "child" })
end)

test("max_ticks stops early and run can continue", function()
    local s = Scheduler.new()
    s:spawn("forever", function(sched) while true do coroutine.yield() end end)
    check_eq(s:run(10), 10)
    check_eq(s:run(5), 15)
    check_eq(s:finished(), {})
end)

test("nothing to run", function()
    check_eq(Scheduler.new():run(), 0)
end)
